name: InstaConsole Universal Core
author: instaconsole

sections.description:
InstaConsole Universal Core helps charities, nonprofits and community groups organise their people and responsibilities in WordPress. Set up departments and reporting lines, appoint team members and give each person a workspace for the responsibilities they accept.

Start with InstaConsole > Master Admin (Start point) and follow the setup checklist. Team members then use My InstaConsole to review and accept responsibilities and open their assigned work areas.

Getting started with Events

If your first goal is to run an event, install and activate Universal Core and the separate InstaConsole Events Manager plugin. In Core, set up your organisation and its Events department, then assign the Events responsibility to the appropriate team member. After accepting it in My InstaConsole, they can open the Events workspace to create an event, set up registration and publish the event listing.

For more information about the plugins, visit InstaConsole.

Main features

  • Organisation and department setup.
  • Staff roles, team membership and responsibility assignments.
  • Responsibility-based staff workspaces and dashboards.
  • Administrative oversight and workflow information.
  • Advisory AI assistance, when configured by an authorised administrator.
  • Integration foundation for InstaConsole Events Manager.
  • Optional WooCommerce My Account navigation integration; WooCommerce is not required.

Optional AI service

AI features require a separately configured OpenAI API key and an external OpenAI account. When an authorised user requests AI guidance, relevant request content may be sent to OpenAI’s API at https://api.openai.com/v1/responses. AI features are optional; normal organisational workflows do not require them. Review the data you send, your organisation’s privacy obligations and OpenAI’s terms and privacy policy: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy/ and https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use/ . API usage may incur charges.

Related InstaConsole plugins

InstaConsole Events Manager adds event proposals, event planning, registrations and public listings. Other separately available commercial modules include Charity Budget Manager Pro, Charity Grants Manager Pro, Charity Accounts Manager Pro, Charity Pledges Manager Pro, Events Manager Pro and Charity Management Suite Pro. These products are not included in this plugin. Find product information at https://instaconsole.com/ .

External Services

OpenAI (optional AI assistant)
When a website administrator supplies an OpenAI API key and tests the connection, the plugin sends a test request to OpenAI. When an authorised user subsequently invokes an AI feature, the plugin sends instructions and task input to the OpenAI Responses API at https://api.openai.com/v1/responses. Depending on the requested task, this input can include organisation context, staff responsibilities, and information entered by the user. The API key is sent to OpenAI for authentication. OpenAI processes these requests according to its applicable terms and privacy practices; API usage may incur separate charges. Core’s basic organisation-management features do not require OpenAI.
OpenAI privacy: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy/
OpenAI API terms: https://openai.com/policies/service-terms/

InstaConsole licence validation (only for separately installed commercial modules)
When an administrator activates, refreshes, or deactivates a licence for a separately installed InstaConsole Pro module, the plugin communicates with the InstaConsole licensing service at https://instaconsole.com/wp-json/ic-lic/v1/. It sends the entered licence key, product identifier, website domain, site URL and locally generated installation identifier. A configured Pro module may also trigger periodic licence-status checks while certain administrative screens are accessed. Universal Core itself does not require a licence or activation with InstaConsole. The licence service is contacted only when commercial modules have registered products and an administrator has entered a licence key. No Pro plugin packages are included or downloaded by this plugin.
InstaConsole privacy: https://instaconsole.com/privacy-policy/
InstaConsole terms: https://instaconsole.com/terms-and-conditions/
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New, search for InstaConsole Universal Core, then install and activate it.
  2. Open InstaConsole > Master Admin (Start point) and follow the setup checklist for the organisation, departments, working structure and team members.
  3. Assign responsibilities and ask staff to review and accept them in My InstaConsole.
  4. Install InstaConsole Events Manager separately if you need event planning, publishing or registrations.
  5. Configure AI settings only if your organisation chooses to use the optional OpenAI service.
sections.faq:
Is WooCommerce required?

No. WooCommerce integration is optional.

Is this suitable for CICs and small charities?

Yes. The organisational features can be used by small community groups and larger nonprofit organisations.

Does Universal Core include Budget, Grants, Accounts or Pledges Pro?

No. These are separate commercial plugins.

Is AI required?

No. AI assistance is optional and requires separate configuration and an external API service.
sections.changelog:
0.13.40.23

  • Add a Profile & Appearance shortcut to the staff dashboard.
  • Include the latest Master Admin setup, 2iC appointment, authority confirmation and Events workspace routing fixes.

0.13.40.15

  • Save Working Structure and matching designations in a single setup form.

0.13.40.14

  • Fix rendering the saved Working Structure summary on the Designations screen.
  • Put the Master Admin setup checklist first and clarify saved Designations and Working Structure status.

0.13.40.12

  • Remove the More Staff Tools placeholder panel from My InstaConsole.

0.13.40.11

  • Send staff login details automatically when a new team account is created.

0.13.40.10

  • Fix security-token validation when saving departments and member types.

0.13.40.6

  • Load plugin scripts and styles through WordPress with per-screen controls and validated browser configuration.
  • Validate organisation and record IDs, enforce AI REST access at the permission callback, and protect audit acknowledgements with a nonce.
  • Keep commercial module expiry messages on the Licences & Updates screen.
  • Use a distinctive prefix for Core declarations while maintaining the published compatibility interfaces and existing storage.
  • Retain the site administrator’s optional OpenAI configuration and the WordPress 6.5 minimum requirement.

0.13.40.4

  • Add request-isolated caching for prepared display-list queries in administrative forms and planning views, with write invalidation and detached result objects.
  • Preserve live permission, approval, handover, audit and save-time validation reads.
  • Record query-specific decisions to keep authoritative/action/report state read-through instead of adding persistent row caches. The optional OpenAI transport still supports WordPress 6.5; the WordPress 7.0 AI Client remains a separate compatibility consideration.
  • Preserve the eight-file plugin layout and all existing public integration contracts.

0.13.40.3

  • Validate organisation selectors as scalar input and preserve action-specific nonce and access checks.
  • Add request-isolated display caches for organisation names, organisation display records, structure summaries and product catalogue rows; writes invalidate them before further reads.
  • Keep permissions, credentials, responsibility state and licence status uncached.
  • Document call-scoped exceptions for necessary custom-table access, guarded schema work; retain unresolved read/write caching advisories.

0.13.40.2

  • Consolidate read-only URL filters into scalar-validated, sanitised input handling while retaining action-specific nonces and access checks.
  • Share positive request-local table metadata and invalidate schema metadata before writes, including shared-module writes.
  • Use WordPress user APIs with explicit cache eviction for fresh onboarding password checks.
  • Combine organisation structure counts without changing readiness rules.
  • Prevent audit organisation ID prefixes matching another organisation and validate decoded organisation ownership before showing audit details.
  • Pass audit selection explicitly instead of rewriting the request global.

0.13.40.1

  • Require an active staff identity and same-organisation active membership when checking explicit responsibility, AI and delegated authority.
  • Cache schema index names only within the current request, clearing metadata at repair/install entry and after every schema alteration.
  • Escape literal table names in schema-existence checks so wildcard characters in database prefixes cannot match other tables.
  • Preserve public interfaces, existing records, permissions and Free Events compatibility.

0.13.40

  • Plugins & Suite separates Free products, WordPress installation and saved licence status; catalogue entries never imply activation.
  • Team form input helper verifies its own nonce, and responsibility assignment helpers receive explicit assignment intent.

  • Request-local schema metadata caching reduces repeated lookups and is invalidated during schema repair.

  • Hardened prepared database queries, request handling, output escaping and password handling.

  • Preserved existing organisational data, public interfaces, licence registration and advisory AI.
  • Repaired standalone staff profile and availability navigation and Free Events AI recognition.
  • Repaired schema formatting for safe WordPress schema comparison and added the nullable shared Events planning link.
  • Protected responsibility saving against missing or malformed payloads and corrected staged-map lookup.
  • Neutralised spreadsheet formulas in availability CSV exports.
